title: An orchestrator and three workers
goal: Split a 3-part feature across three worktrees with explicit file ownership, hand off through files, and merge with no conflicts.
setup_cmd: cp -r exercises/ex-5-2-team/starter ~/fm-ex/ex-5-2-team && cd ~/fm-ex/ex-5-2-team && npm i && git init -b main && git add -A && git commit -m starter

starter_prompts.claude: You are the orchestrator. Read SPEC.md and the tests in tests/. Do not write any feature code. Propose OWNERSHIP.json: three workers (parser, grouper, renderer) with a branch each and one explicit owned file each, and src/index.mjs for me. Then write a worker brief for each: owned file, spec section, the frozen test file, and the handoffs/<name>.md format from SPEC.md. Show me both before anything runs.
starter_prompts.codex: You are the orchestrator. Read SPEC.md and the tests in tests/. Do not write any feature code. Propose OWNERSHIP.json: three workers (parser, grouper, renderer) with a branch each and one explicit owned file each, and src/index.mjs for me. Then write a worker brief for each: owned file, spec section, the frozen test file, and the handoffs/<name>.md format from SPEC.md. Show me both before anything runs.

solution_notes: Ownership is by explicit file, decided and committed before any worker starts. Three workers each own one file under src/, so their branches cannot touch the same lines and the merges are trivial.
The glue file src/index.mjs belongs to the orchestrator and is written after the merges. It depends on all three parts, so no worker can own it without waiting on the others.
The tests are frozen for everyone. They are the contract between the parts, so a worker who finds one wrong reports it in the handoff instead of editing it.
Handoffs are files with real test output. The orchestrator reads a note, not a transcript, and the ownership test checks the notes exist.
